planningDefault.classification: Configurable AGOS service-planning assumption, not measured Calapan demand, a universal WHO requirement, a medical prescription, or a current shortage observation
planningDefault.formula: reported affected people * (selected drinking litres/person/day + selected food-preparation litres/person/day) * requested days; subtract verified usable water already available where applicable
planningDefault.sourceTitle: WHO Technical Note 9: How much water is needed in emergencies, updated July 2013
planningDefault.secondarySourceLocation: WASH Standard 2.1 table printed page 107 (PDF page 132); Appendix 3 printed page 145 (PDF page 170)

sourceRanges.survivalIntakeScope: Drinking plus water contained in food; depends on climate and individual physiology
sourceRanges.cookingScope: Water used for food preparation, separate from food moisture consumed; depends on food type and social/cultural norms

planningDefault.avoidDoubleCounting: WHO survival intake already includes water in food. The selected 3-litre drinking component is an AGOS distribution allowance informed by that intake range, not a claim that all intake must be drunk. The separate 3-litre preparation component is water used to prepare food, not another allowance for food moisture. Do not add food moisture again.
planningDefault.notes: The 6-litre total is an application choice: 3 litres allocated for drinking and the lower end (3 litres) of WHO basic-cooking range. WHO and Sphere do not define 6 litres as a universal standard. Planners should adjust for heat, activity, health needs and food preparation, with human review. The broader 15-litre domestic-water benchmark includes hygiene and is not the default for this app. Do not infer shortage, priority, affected people or delivery entitlement from census population alone.
